title: Signed totalization and strict-transition square for normalized coefficient comparisons
statement:
Let $u:\operatorname{Sh}(\mathcal X)\to\operatorname{Sh}(\mathcal Y)$ be a geometric morphism of small sites, with $u^{-1}\dashv u_*$ and $u^{-1}$ left exact. For $W=X,Y$, let $R_{W,\bullet}^0,R_{W,\bullet}^1$ be inverse sequences of commutative ring sheaves and $i_W:R_W^0\to R_W^1$ maps of inverse sequences. Let $\phi^a:u^{-1}R_Y^a\to R_X^a$ be compatible with the sequence maps and satisfy $i_X\phi^0=\phi^1u^{-1}i_Y$. Use module sheaves [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category] and actual sheafified tensors [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product]. Put $F_aM=R_X^a\otimes_{u^{-1}R_Y^a}u^{-1}M$ and $S_WM=R_W^1\otimes_{R_W^0}M$.
All formulas for $F,S$ are now levelwise. A strict system consists of arbitrary, possibly unbounded $\mathbf Z$-indexed cochain complexes with semilinear chain transitions for the given ring transitions; a strict morphism commutes with all these transitions. Let $K,H$ be such systems over $R_{Y,\bullet}^0$, or over $R_{W,\bullet}^0$ when only $s_W$ is used. Write $T_a$ for the signed direct-sum total tensor [def-pc-tensor-complex-sheaves], whose differential on $x\in K^p$ is $dx\otimes y+(-1)^p x\otimes dy$. Suppose at each level the natural module isomorphisms $k,s_W$ have the four prescriptions of [lem-pur-coefficient-comparisons-balanced-construction]. Write $c_a:F_aT_a\cong T_a(F_a,F_a)$ for the fixed normalized comparisons [lem-pur-cochain-pullback-tensor-coherence].

The degreewise $k$ and direct sums of $s_W$ are natural chain isomorphisms $S_XF_0\cong F_1S_Y$ and $S_WT_0\cong T_1(S_W,S_W)$; both maps and inverses commute separately with $d\otimes1$ and $(-1)^p1\otimes d$. The same assertions hold for $c_a$. All these maps and their inverses commute with arbitrary semilinear sequence transitions and hence are isomorphisms of strict systems. More precisely, for a transition $m\to n$, denote the ring maps by $\rho_W^a$ and the input chain transitions by $t_K,t_H$. After either order of comparison and transition the values are respectively
$$\rho_X^1(b)i_{X,n}(\rho_X^0(a))\otimes(1\otimes t_Kx),\qquad
\rho_X^1(b)\phi_n^1(u^{-1}\rho_Y^1(d))\otimes(1\otimes t_Kx),$$
$$(\rho_W^1(b)\otimes t_Kx)\otimes(1\otimes t_Hy),\qquad
\rho_W^1(b)\rho_W^1(d)\otimes(t_Kx\otimes t_Hy)$$
for $k,k^{-1},s_W,s_W^{-1}$, and $(\rho_X^a(a)\otimes t_Kx)\otimes(1\otimes t_Hy)$ for $c_a$.

The following equality holds in strict cochain systems, including its inverse equality:
$$c_1F_1(s_Y)k_{T_0(K,H)}=T_1(k_K,k_H)s_XS_X(c_0).$$
On the full generator $b\otimes(a\otimes(x\otimes y))$, both routes have value $(b i_X(a)\otimes(1\otimes x))\otimes(1\otimes(1\otimes y))$. These assertions concern whole unbounded direct-sum totals, with every sequence transition retained, without flatness, bounds, or invertibility of transition adjoints.

proof.text: The kappa differential equations are the hom and inverse naturality equations of its module natural isomorphism, applied separately to each signed differential map. For tensor comparisons, prove generically in additive monoidal categories that a map with the stated summand values commutes separately with D1 and D2. Test a coproduct inclusion; tensor naturality proves D1, and additivity preserves the integer sign in D2. Outside adjacent degrees both maps are zero. Apply this generic lemma to the inverse total comparison, then cancel the isomorphism for its forward direction. This handles arbitrary unbounded complexes and negative degrees.
